title: When you spend hundreds, thousand dollars for a game, do you expect some returns or you just like to dev games?
author: bioshock73
selftext: If you expect money, what is your strategy for porfitmaximalization?

comments.author: Any-Blacksmith-2054
comments.body: I don't expect any money, but I spend just $20

replies.author: TopIntelligent8802
replies.body: so you only spend 20 a month, which means you spend more, or are you developing your game for only one month?

replies.author: Any-Blacksmith-2054
replies.body: I jsu started 2 weeks ago, not sure if I will prolong

replies.author: TopIntelligent8802
replies.body: thats how i started. Now i have three ultra accounts

comments.author: Putrid_Clue_2127
comments.body: I guess it depends on the purpose for building the game and your current financial situation. For me, I'm building the game for myself. That was always my goal. Although after the last few months I've actually come to enjoy the designing and testing process of building the game just as much as actually playing it. So as long as I enjoy the game in the end, that's my goal. That being said, I do release videos, shorts, and updates on different platforms to see how much interest there is out there in what I'm building. This also lets people know it exists for when launch day comes. So far the increase in views and likes each video is telling me I'm on the right track. So if other people buy it when the time comes, that'll just be extra awesome!

replies.author: bioshock73
replies.body: Without ingame mini transactions, is it possible?

replies.author: StoneCypher
replies.body: not an expert, but as i understand it, the simplest case is the purchase price.  dlc is next, extension then cosmetic then extracting (like gacha).  followed by subscription (battle pass, etc) then ads then donation

replies.author: bioshock73
replies.body: Purchase price is free becazse of mobile game.

replies.author: StoneCypher
replies.body: this just in: freemium is not the best option on mobile

comments.author: Fun-Sundae4060
comments.body:
Profitmaxxing is the goal.

Ads, high CTR, monetization ladders that scale up and never end, and a fun core loop. I develop on Roblox

replies.author: Fun-Sundae4060
replies.body: A/B test a bunch of different styles of thumbnails and pick the best styles and copy front-page game thumbnails

comments.author: blackskies69
comments.body: For me its a hobby until it's not. Right now I'm just having fun making lots of games.

comments.author: PoisonSD
comments.body: Profit and building something is the goal

comments.author: True_Woodpecker2118
comments.body: Nah, im making my dream game for me, its very niche, the only monetisation is extra boost packs, that give a very generous amount for what you can do in it. Id rather players build up. Thats the whole point of the game. The buildup.

comments.author: velocimposter
comments.body:
Make a game that has an audience, make a game that has soul.  Unless you can meet those basic goals you will never truly reach the top.

If you are purely in game development for money and don't have a vision, first I'd ask why TF are you in game development...  then why are you not making tools or other software that is much more cut and dry.

comments.author: TheLastNeonDev
comments.body: kept the costs low, the cantonese voices are tts on a free tier so i only do like 10 lines a day lol. been at it 5 months and the demo is planned for next fest in february, so no idea yet if it makes anything

comments.author: HouseOfWyrd
comments.body:
There's no trick to making a successful game.

That doesn't mean it's easy and AI doesn't make it that much easier.
